name: Paspalum
common_group: Paspalums — six existing Hays County Botany learner species

project_scope.selection_mode: existing manifest species FINISH/ENRICH (no new first-card admission)
project_scope.taxonomic_review: Species-level identity and native-by-county audit remain as they were; this is a structural visual learner pass, not new verification.

look_here_first: Start with how the SEEDHEAD IS BUILT. Most paspalums carry flattened oval SPIKELETS in a row or paired rows on ONE SIDE of each fingerlike RACEME. Count racemes on one intact flowering stem and photograph their ATTACHMENT; then inspect the WHOLE ROOTED PLANT (low wetland stolon vs large bunchgrass) and a true leaf collar/ligule. Do NOT assume two racemes means knotgrass or 10 racemes automatically means vaseygrass.
shared_morphology: Paspalum usually has one or more unilateral, spike-like reproductive RACEMES; each raceme is a branch of the full inflorescence.
Green oval compressed units seen on these racemes are SPIKELETS, each with distinct glumes/sterile and fertile florets; purple flower parts may protrude during anthesis.
A grass leaf consists of blade, basal sheath and a ligule at their junction. Correct collar photography requires blade/sheath movement rather than a distant tuft photo.
A mature measured spikelet macro plus habitat/growth habit and a complete raceme count is often required for species-level separation.

study_strategy.priority: Photo-led field recognition first, reproductive anatomy second
crew_sequence: 1. Look for a low runner versus stout perennial tuft before examining the seedhead.
2. Count one-sided racemes attached to ONE culm; distinguish full head from a single raceme.
3. Follow ONE raceme face-on; show the rows of green flattened spikelets and where purple/black anthers project.
4. Examine whole-plant leaves, basal nodes, sheaths and the membranous ligule.
5. Compare mature measured spikelets under magnification; do not force certainty from panicle silhouette or name label.

six_species_field_key.field_hint: Wet-ground creeping perennial with rooted STOLONS; usually TWO (occasionally three) racemes diverge as a V
six_species_field_key.next_check: Show true rooted node, two unilateral branch spikelet rows, mature spikelet versus P. notatum

six_species_field_key.field_hint: Generally smaller, one to a FEW racemes, with varieties differing in leaf hairiness
six_species_field_key.next_check: Whole head and leaf hair/ligule characters; tiny flattened spikelet and floral details; no variety from photo alone

six_species_field_key.field_hint: Usually several racemes with tight oval flattened spikelet pairs about 2.7–3.2 mm in references
six_species_field_key.next_check: Upper-glume fine hairs, spikelet size, full raceme count and collar; source photo only shows one fragment

six_species_field_key.field_hint: Robust large upright grass clump; often a few LONG racemes and larger rounded oval spikelets
six_species_field_key.next_check: Head and mature oval roughly 3.5–5 mm spikelet photos; current canonical photo only shows bunch habit

six_species_field_key.field_hint: Coarse dallisgrass, generally several (often 3–7) racemes, hairy larger about 3–4 mm spikelets
six_species_field_key.next_check: Measure multiple mature silky-margined spikelets; compare entire head with vaseygrass

six_species_field_key.field_hint: Tall coarse introduced vaseygrass, generally MANY (commonly 10–20) slender racemes on elongated axis
six_species_field_key.next_check: Measure smaller roughly 2–3 mm edge-hairy spikelets, check true basal plant and collar; count overlaps

six_species_field_key.field_hint: Head fragment, overlap, juvenile flowering stage or missing collar/mature spikelets
six_species_field_key.next_check: Label Paspalum sp. pending properly documented flowering mature specimens

comparison_cards.title: Dallisgrass versus vaseygrass
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Count racemes attached to the WHOLE head and examine measured marginally hairy spikelets.

field_matrix.dilatatum: Coarse clumping grass, often around 1 m
field_matrix.urvillei: Usually taller robust grass, often 1–2.5 m

field_matrix.dilatatum: Larger around 3–4 mm with conspicuous long silky margin hairs
field_matrix.urvillei: Smaller around 2–3 mm with hairs at margin

comparison_cards.stop_rule: Don't classify without a complete head and several measured spikelets; height and branch counts overlap.

comparison_cards.title: Knotgrass versus thin paspalum
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Trace actual creeping stolon nodes and check full flowering head/leaf hairiness.

field_matrix.setaceum: More variable leafy growth with varieties needing foliage inspection

field_matrix.distichum: Typically two terminal V-shaped unilateral racemes
field_matrix.setaceum: Often one to a few unilateral branches; can look close
Leaf hairs, measured small spikelets, collar

comparison_cards.stop_rule: Two racemes alone do not prove knotgrass; P. notatum is also an important outside-genus-card look-alike.

comparison_cards.title: Florida paspalum versus pubiflorum
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Measure mature spikelets and show the COMPLETE head, don't just compare plant size.

field_matrix.clue: Often large coarser upright clump and larger rounded mature spikelets
Several racemes and smaller roughly 2.7–3.2 mm oval spikelets, glumes variable pubescence

comparison_cards.stop_rule: Present floridanum photo lacks seedhead; pubiflorum photo lacks the whole head and glume hairs. Both are provisional photo ID cues.

visual_comparison.title: Paspalum — six species, real photos of racemes, spikelets, and growth habit
visual_comparison.subtitle: Seven original credited images from all six installed learner entries. Browser arrow annotations point to visible parts only, never unseen rooting nodes or spikelet hairs.
visual_comparison.memory_rule: WHOLE HEAD then ONE RACEME then ONE SPIKELET. Rooted stolons matter. Number of seedhead fingers is a clue, not a final diagnosis.

visual_comparison.overlay_note: Seven photographs are existing exact-source archive files; artist/photographer, URL and license copied from their current species cards. No new image bytes installed. Site license filtering and noncommercial terms apply. Dallisgrass collar photo marks visible blade/sheath/hair region; not a ligule measurement. Floridanum has a basal tuft image only. Pubiflorum and setaceum do not have measured reproductive macro evidence; source taxon IDs still provisional.
